## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

# MANIAC MANSION REIMAGINED — 10s CONTINUOUS 2D PANORAMIC SHOT

## 1. VISUAL STYLE

Create one continuous 10-second cinematic shot in the exact visual style of the reference images.

Modernized 2D cartoon point-and-click adventure aesthetic, clean outlines, rich colors, soft shading, subtle gradients, detailed painted backgrounds and atmospheric nighttime lighting.

Preserve the visual identity, geometry, proportions, colors and details of the reference environments throughout the entire sequence.

All landscape references represent different views of ONE continuous, pre-existing 2D panoramic environment.

Do not treat reference images as separate scenes.

Do not morph between reference images.

## 2. REFERENCE IMAGES

- `<Picture 1>` — Initial landscape: bare tree on the right, without meteor.
- `<Picture 2>` — Initial landscape with meteor: reference for meteor scale, starting position and direction.
- `<Picture 3>` — Grassy hill before meteor impact.
- `<Picture 4>` — The exact same hill after impact, with the crater.
- `<Picture 5>` — Final landscape containing the Victorian mansion.
- `<Picture 6>` — Isolated meteor: reference for rocky body, flames and fiery tail.
- `<Picture 7>` — Isolated turquoise moon: reference for appearance.

Pictures 1–5 define successive camera compositions within the SAME fixed environment.

Pictures 6–7 define isolated visual assets, NOT separate scenes.

## 3. CORE WORLD RULE — FIXED 2D PANORAMA

The environment is one continuous, completely static 2D panoramic background.

It contains grassy hills, tall grass, stones, bare trees, stars, a turquoise moon and a distant Victorian mansion.

Every element already exists at its fixed position in the world.

The camera reveals different parts of this existing panorama through horizontal movement.

**The background is a flat 2D illustration, not a three-dimensional environment.**

All landscape elements must retain their exact size, shape, position and proportions.

No geometry reconstruction, scaling, morphing or perspective transformation is allowed.

The meteor crater is the only permanent modification to the terrain.

## 4. CAMERA — PURE HORIZONTAL TRANSLATION

One uninterrupted horizontal camera tracking movement toward the LEFT.

The fixed panoramic background scrolls horizontally toward the RIGHT.

Camera movement is equivalent to moving a rectangular viewport horizontally across a large static 2D illustration.

The camera maintains:

- Constant scale.
- Constant height.
- Constant orientation.
- Constant focal length.
- Constant perspective.
- No zoom.
- No dolly-in or dolly-out.
- No push-in or pull-back.
- No rotation.
- No vertical movement.
- No perspective shift.
- No depth-based scaling.

**No parallax between landscape layers.**

Every static background element scrolls horizontally at the same speed.

The camera begins stationary, gradually accelerates, maintains smooth horizontal movement and gently slows toward the final composition.

Objects may enter or leave the frame only through the left or right edge as a consequence of this movement.

## 5. TERRAIN GEOMETRY LOCK — CRITICAL

All hills belong to the same fixed 2D background illustration.

Their geometry is permanently locked.

During the travelling, every hill must retain exactly the same:

- Size and scale.
- Silhouette.
- Slope.
- Height.
- Crest shape.
- Horizon position within the panorama.
- Position relative to neighboring hills.
- Surrounding stones and vegetation.

**Hills are only allowed to translate horizontally across the screen.**

No hill may grow, shrink, stretch, compress, inflate, collapse or change perspective.

No hill may move toward or away from the camera.

Never resize hills to connect reference images.

Never create temporary terrain to fill gaps between references.

No additional hill, mound, ridge or slope may appear during the travelling.

Terrain continuity must be achieved exclusively through horizontal scrolling of the fixed panorama.

## 6. TREE AND VEGETATION STABILITY

The initial bare tree from `<Picture 1>` is already present on the right side of the frame.

It remains permanently rooted to its original hill.

As the camera moves LEFT, the tree moves toward the RIGHT edge of the screen and naturally exits the frame.

The tree never changes size, silhouette or proportions.

Its trunk and roots remain fixed.

Only its thin branches may sway slightly in the wind.

Do not generate new trees during the travelling.

Do not generate temporary trees in the middle distance or background.

Other vegetation may only appear if it already belongs to the referenced environment and enters naturally through the frame edge.

Tall grass may gently sway without altering the shape of the terrain.

## 7. MOON — STRICT SCREEN-SPACE CONTINUITY

The moon uses the exact visual appearance of `<Picture 7>`.

The moon is a permanent, fixed element of the panoramic sky.

**At the beginning of the sequence, the moon is completely OUTSIDE THE FRAME, to the LEFT.**

The moon is initially invisible.

As the camera travels LEFT, the moon enters the visible frame progressively through the LEFT edge.

Its rightmost edge becomes visible first.

The rest of the moon gradually enters the frame as the camera continues moving.

Once visible, the moon moves horizontally toward the RIGHT side of the screen at the same scrolling speed as the fixed panoramic background.

The moon remains perfectly round, with constant size, colors and details.

Never introduce the moon directly in the center of the frame.

Never make the moon pop in, fade in, teleport or suddenly change position.

Never regenerate the moon after it becomes visible.

The moon must remain continuously visible until it naturally exits the frame, if the camera travels far enough.

## 8. CONTINUOUS TIMELINE

### 00:00–00:02 — INITIAL LANDSCAPE AND METEOR

Begin with the exact composition of `<Picture 1>`.

The bare tree stands on the right side of the grassy hill.

The camera is initially stationary.

Only the thin branches and tall grass sway gently in the nighttime wind.

At approximately 00:01, ONE small meteor enters the upper-right part of the sky.

Match its initial scale and position to `<Picture 2>`.

Match its detailed rocky appearance and fiery trail to `<Picture 6>`.

The meteor moves diagonally downward from RIGHT to LEFT.

Its orange-red flames flicker naturally, producing a few small glowing particles.

The meteor is the only rapidly moving object independent of the camera.

### 00:02–00:05 — CONTINUOUS LEFTWARD TRAVELLING

The camera begins a smooth horizontal translation toward the LEFT.

The entire fixed panoramic background scrolls toward the RIGHT at a uniform speed.

The initial tree gradually exits through the RIGHT edge.

The grassy landscape shown in `<Picture 3>` progressively enters from the LEFT.

All hills retain their original sizes and silhouettes.

No perspective change, zoom or parallax is allowed.

Do not enlarge or shrink any hill.

Do not introduce new hills, trees or background elements.

The meteor continues its diagonal descent toward the target hill.

The turquoise moon from `<Picture 7>` enters progressively from the LEFT edge when the travelling reaches its fixed position.

It must never appear suddenly in the middle of the screen.

### 00:05–00:07 — METEOR IMPACT

The meteor strikes the grassy hill from `<Picture 3>`.

A brief localized orange flash illuminates the immediate impact area.

A small amount of soil and a few stones are displaced.

A crater forms at the exact impact point.

The resulting crater matches `<Picture 4>` in shape, size and position.

**CRITICAL POST-IMPACT GEOMETRY LOCK:**

Only the impact zone changes.

The hill's overall silhouette, slope, height and surrounding terrain remain unchanged.

The impact must not generate secondary hills, bumps, mounds or ridges.

No temporary hill may appear before, during or after the impact.

Once the crater is formed, the terrain becomes completely stable again.

The crater remains fixed, with faint smoke and a subtle residual orange glow.

The camera continues its uninterrupted leftward travelling.

The surrounding terrain moves exclusively through horizontal scrolling, with no change of scale.

### 00:07–00:10 — MANSION REVEAL

The camera continues moving LEFT.

The Victorian mansion from `<Picture 5>` progressively enters the frame through the LEFT edge.

The mansion already exists in the panorama.

It is revealed by camera movement only.

Preserve its exact architecture:

- Number of floors.
- Towers.
- Roof structure.
- Windows.
- Building silhouette.
- Proportions.
- Surrounding vegetation.

The mansion must not change size during the travelling.

No reconstruction, morphing or architectural transformation.

#### WINDOW LIGHTING — ONE BY ONE

As the mansion becomes visible, a few previously dark windows begin illuminating.

Windows light up individually, **ONE AT A TIME**.

Use an irregular and unpredictable order across different floors and different parts of the building.

Avoid systematic left-to-right or bottom-to-top patterns.

Introduce unequal time intervals between each activation.

Never illuminate multiple new windows simultaneously.

Each illuminated window remains lit.

#### WINDOW BRIGHTNESS

The window illumination must be approximately 50% dimmer than strong interior lighting.

Use a soft, warm, muted yellow color.

Keep illumination subtle, natural and atmospheric.

Minimal bloom.

Minimal light spill onto exterior walls.

No strong glow, flashes or overexposed windows.

Do not illuminate every window.

The camera gradually slows and settles into the final composition of `<Picture 5>`.

The final image remains stable.

## 9. ALLOWED ANIMATIONS — EXHAUSTIVE LIST

Only the following elements may animate independently of the camera:

1. Thin tree branches gently swaying in the wind.
2. Tall grass subtly moving in the wind.
3. The meteor flying diagonally, with animated flames and glowing particles.
4. Localized meteor impact, crater formation, small debris and faint residual smoke.
5. Mansion window lights turning on individually, in an irregular sequence, with soft low-intensity illumination.

All other elements remain completely static.

Stars do not move or twinkle.

Clouds do not move independently.

The moon does not pulse, fade, deform or move independently.

Hills do not change size or shape.

Tree trunks remain fixed.

Mansion architecture remains unchanged.

The horizontal scrolling caused by camera movement is not an independent object animation.

## 10. SOUNDTRACK AND SOUND EFFECTS

Create a mysterious cinematic soundtrack inspired by the retro-synth atmosphere of the original Maniac Mansion introduction, modernized with subtle orchestral textures.

**00:00–00:02:** quiet mysterious synth atmosphere, faint nighttime wind.

**00:02–00:05:** gradual musical crescendo, subtle meteor whoosh.

**00:05–00:07:** short deep impact sound synchronized with the crash, followed by faint crackling embers.

**00:07–00:10:** atmospheric mysterious musical theme accompanying the mansion reveal.

Add subtle wind and grass rustling throughout the sequence.

No dialogue, voiceover, narration or singing.

## 11. NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS

No cuts or scene transitions.

No zoom or perspective changes.

No parallax.

No depth-based scaling.

No hill resizing.

No temporary hills.

No new trees.

No temporary trees.

No scenery appearing suddenly in the center of the frame.

No sudden moon appearance or disappearance.

No landscape reconstruction.

No image morphing.

No second meteor.

No secondary impact.

No exaggerated explosion.

No simultaneous mansion window illumination.

No excessive window brightness or bloom.

No additional characters, buildings or objects.

No text, subtitles, logos or overlays.

Full-frame 16:9 composition without black borders.

## 12. FINAL PRIORITY

**The sequence must behave exactly like a fixed, flat 2D panoramic illustration viewed through a horizontally scrolling camera.**

Every hill, tree, stone, cloud, star, moon and building maintains a constant size and fixed world position.

The camera only reveals existing scenery.

The moon must enter gradually from the LEFT edge.

The initial tree must exit naturally through the RIGHT edge.

No temporary tree or hill may appear.

No hill may grow or shrink during travelling.

The crater is the only permanent terrain modification.

Mansion windows illuminate ONE AT A TIME in an irregular sequence, using soft warm light at approximately half normal brightness.

**Prioritize geometric stability, spatial continuity and consistent 2D scrolling over visual complexity.**


**Background music:** A mysterious, eerie, and slightly whimsical 1980s point-and-click adventure game soundtrack, inspired by the atmosphere of Maniac Mansion.

Retro cinematic horror-comedy music featuring vintage analog synthesizers, haunting melodies, deep atmospheric bass, subtle electronic percussion, and playful spooky motifs.

Begin with a quiet, suspenseful atmosphere, gradually building tension as the camera travels across the moonlit landscape.

As the mansion comes into view, introduce a darker, more dramatic musical theme with ominous synthesizer chords and a memorable, slightly quirky melody.

The music should evoke mystery, supernatural adventure, dark humor, and nostalgic 1980s video game aesthetics.

**Instrumental only. No vocals, no dialogue.** Avoid modern electronic dance music, epic orchestral scores, and aggressive horror sound effects.
